ErrorEnvelope.description: Plain error envelope `{ error }` used by most routes. `error` is a human-readable message.

gstNumber.description: 15-char GSTIN matching ^[0-9]{2}[A-Z]{5}[0-9]{4}[A-Z][1-9A-Z]Z[0-9A-Z]$, or null/"" to clear

reason.description: Why the vendor is being flagged

leadId.description: Lead this flag relates to; null when not order-specific

UnspecifiedObject.description: Response body shape not captured by the source re-audit (only the status code was detected). Any JSON object.

imageName.description: gstin | gumasta | aadharudhyog | shopimg | shopphoto | pancardimg | aadharcardimgfront | aadharcardimgback | selfphoto, or the raw column name (gstinImage, panCardImage, ...)

url.description: Publicly reachable URL of the uploaded document image

allowedSlots.description: Array of canonical slot strings; empty array = all slots

MessageEnvelope.description: Message-only envelope `{ message }`; used for both success and failure responses.

SuccessMessageErrorEnvelope.description: Error envelope `{ success: false, message, error }`.

SuccessMessageEnvelope.description: Envelope `{ success, message }`; `success` is `true` on 2xx and `false` on error responses.

Unauthorized.description: Unauthenticated - no valid admin session (NextAuth cookie), or the expected token/secret is missing or wrong. For operations whose description says *reconstructed from source*, only the status code was detected in the audit; the body shape shown is the codebase convention, not verified per route.

Forbidden.description: Forbidden - the session is valid but the role is not allowed to do this. For operations whose description says *reconstructed from source*, only the status code was detected in the audit; the body shape shown is the codebase convention, not verified per route.

InternalServerError.description: Internal server error - unhandled failure inside the route handler. For operations whose description says *reconstructed from source*, only the status code was detected in the audit; the body shape shown is the codebase convention, not verified per route.

BadRequest.description: Bad request / validation error - a required field is missing or invalid. For operations whose description says *reconstructed from source*, only the status code was detected in the audit; the body shape shown is the codebase convention, not verified per route.

NotFound.description: Not found - the referenced record does not exist. For operations whose description says *reconstructed from source*, only the status code was detected in the audit; the body shape shown is the codebase convention, not verified per route.

Conflict.description: Conflict - the record already exists or its current state does not allow this change. For operations whose description says *reconstructed from source*, only the status code was detected in the audit; the body shape shown is the codebase convention, not verified per route.

cookieAuth.name: next-auth.session-token
cookieAuth.description: NextAuth JWT session cookie from logging in to the admin panel. On HTTPS the cookie name is `__Secure-next-auth.session-token`.

cronBearer.description: `LINODE_CRON_SECRET` as a bearer token — every cron job goes through `assertCronAuth` in `lib/linode/cron-auth.ts`, which reads only this variable (despite some jobs being non-Linode).

unverifiedAccessToken.name: Authorization
unverifiedAccessToken.description: Legacy customer routes: an `accessToken` cookie or an `Authorization` header must be PRESENT, but the value is never verified. Not real authentication.

adsWebhookSecret.name: x-webhook-secret
adsWebhookSecret.description: `ADS_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, sent either as the `x-webhook-secret` header or as a `secret` field in the JSON body. If the env var is unset the route rejects every call with 401 (it does not fall through to unauthenticated access).

webhookSecret.name: x-webhook-secret
webhookSecret.description: Generic `x-webhook-secret` header check for an inbound webhook.

cronSecretBearer.description: `CRON_SECRET` as a bearer token, compared with `bearerMatches` in `lib/auth/secret-compare.ts`. Distinct from `cronBearer`, which uses `LINODE_CRON_SECRET`.
